s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls with otologic abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Obstructed external ear canals with effusion and cerumen
Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals
key_facts: 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry
Presented to the emergency department with progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls
Initial fall resulted in a nasal bridge laceration
No prior medical history
Alert and afebrile on examination
External ear canals obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Three-month history of ear problems
Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
Partial resolution with antibiotic treatment
Current otoscopic examination showed intact left tympanic membrane and occluded right external canal
Frenzel’s examination showed no nystagmus
Contrast-enhanced CT showed bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals
Adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated profound right-sided hearing loss

differentials: Langerhans cell histiocytosis variant with osteolytic lesions
per_call: Langerhans cell histiocytosis variant with osteolytic lesions

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals, with otologic abnormalities and hearing loss

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to Langerhans cell histiocytosis, with possible involvement of the temporal bone

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: Occluded right external canal with polypoid tissue and purulent secretion, suggesting a possible cholesteatoma

shortlist.label: Mastoiditis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and history of ear problems, including otitis media with effusion

shortlist.label: Gorham-Stout disease
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions in the mastoids and semicircular canals, with possible involvement of the temporal bone
